name: TurboRAG: Accelerating Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Precomputed KV Caches for Chunked Text
problem: Conventional RAG concatenates many retrieved chunks and prefills all of them online, and since prefill is the most compute-dense step in the whole serving stack, this dominates time-to-first-token.
mechanism: Inverts the paradigm: precompute and store each document's KV cache OFFLINE, then at inference time directly RETRIEVE the saved KV cache for prefill instead of running the prefill over the chunk text. Online KV computation is eliminated entirely. The non-obvious part is that this is not a no-op, and the paper's actual contribution is the bookkeeping: attention mask semantics (each chunk needs INDEPENDENT attention rather than joint attention over the concatenation) and POSITION ID remapping for the concatenated KV caches, because positions baked into an offline cache are contiguous-per-document and must be remapped to their real slots at query time. The authors then FINE-TUNE the LM to tolerate the resulting attention and position-ID pattern, which is the honest cost of the approach - it is not a training-free swap.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim: reduces time-to-first-token by up to 9.4x versus conventional RAG systems (8.6x on average) across a suite of RAG benchmarks, while reserving comparable accuracy. Two honest qualifiers the reader needs: the baseline is a CONVENTIONAL RAG SYSTEM, not a modern engine with prefix caching enabled, and the comparable-accuracy claim requires the authors' fine-tuning - which is why the paper's own summary lists it as contribution 5 rather than an aside.

An ARR submission is a REVIEW BATCH, not a publication: a paper can sit in an ARR batch indefinitely without appearing in any proceedings volume, so citing ACL ARR as its venue would be exactly the confident-wrong-answer failure this repo has shipped twice. diverged - so the honest position was never 'unpublished', it was 'not yet published as of the search date'.

THE PUBLISHER'S OWN DEPOSIT (source w6p-aclanthology-2025-emnlp-main-334-turborag): ACL Anthology
2025.emnlp-main.334, volume 'Proceedings of the 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language
Processing', pages 6588-6601, Suzhou China, November 2025, venue EMNLP, SIG SIGDAT, publisher ACL, DOI
10.18653/v1/2025.emnlp-main.334, bibkey lu-etal-2025-turborag. Identification is EXACT on both axes: the title
matches character for character and all FIVE authors (Songshuo Lu, Hua Wang, Yutian Rong, Zhi Chen, Yaohua
Tang) match the arXiv API response for 2410.07590 in the same order.

THE CAMERA-READY ABSTRACT DIFFERS FROM THE ARXIV ABSTRACT, and the difference is a MECHANISM claim rather than
wording, so it is worth carrying. arXiv v1 says the system 'fine-tune[s] a pretrained language model to maintain
model accuracy'; the Anthology version describes a hybrid offline-online paradigm that pre-computes chunk-level
KV caches, stitches them at inference using INDEPENDENT-ATTENTION and REORDERED-RoPE techniques, and
'preserves answer quality WITHOUT CHANGING THE MODEL ARCHITECTURE'. So the published version is strictly
stronger: no model fine-tuning required. A reader holding only the arXiv PDF gets the weaker story and never
sees the two named techniques. The 9.4x max / 8.6x mean TTFT reduction against conventional RAG is identical in
both.
